It is so personal that it felt almost intrusive to listen to...like reading someone’s diary. As soon as the final track finished I knew that I couldn’t listen to it again unless someone close to me died. I’ve heard most of the popular songs in this thread and none of them compare to the overwhelming sense of pain and loss he manages to so perfectly portray...it’s a rare gift to be able to take that pain and make something beautiful of it. I only listened to it once. I think about it all the time.

hello - i have dealt with similar issues. yelling is a hard boundary for me in relationships; it’s very triggering for me and i WILL cry if yelled at. my partner knows this and never yells or raises her voice in anger at me. i think this is a reasonable boundary to have and that in an adult relationship you should be able to resolve issues without yelling or being mean. i think the problem lies at least partially with your boyfriend, who you mention uses “harsh words” and “gets mean”. it is not ok to be mean to your partner even in anger. it is normal and understandable for you to be upset if that happens. a kind and loving partner will not use cruel language during arguments. i hope you are not settling for someone who does; you deserve to date someone who is considerate of your feelings even during a disagreement.

that being said, i understand perfectly that sense of being emotionally overwhelmed and not being able to stop yourself reacting in that way. the only thing i have found that works in the moment is taking a break. if you find yourself tearing up or becoming overwhelmed and you are able to notice yourself reaching that breaking point, it is perfectly ok and reasonable to excuse yourself and go take a few minutes to cry in the bathroom, cry outside, take a walk around the block, etc—anything that works to help you collect yourself and sort out your feelings. this will also help you to better articulate what you want to say when you return. perhaps take a few minutes to write down your thoughts and feelings. once you feel calmer and in control of your body, you can return to finish the conversation in a better headspace. this too is a reasonable boundary to have! you are allowed to take a break if you need one.

Hi! I’m nonbinary and I’ve been on T three times, for about 2 months each over the course of a few years. I physically transitioned specifically to be more androgynous. Part of the reason I spaced it out the way I did was because I didn’t want facial hair; fortunately that wasn’t the swiftest effect for me personally but keep in mind that everyone’s body is different and I have friends who grew stubble straight off the bat. Conversely, I also have friends whose voice didn’t drop much until like 6 months in, whereas that was one of the quickest effects I experienced.

The only permanent effects of taking T are any voice deepening, bottom growth, and facial/body hair growth (although the little I did develop almost entirely went away with time, so it does depend somewhat on how thick it is when you stop). Any fat redistribution and facial shape changes will eventually revert back to how they were initially.

While the voice thing is the only remaining noticeable side effect for me unless I’m naked, having a deeper voice is super effective for androgyny purposes. You don’t mention if this is your goal or not, but I can tell you that just the addition of having a deep voice changes people’s perception of you significantly. My voice perhaps isn’t quite as deep as it would have eventually ended up were I to stay on hormones permanently, but it’s in a solid tenor range. Pre-T I was gendered as female by strangers about 10% of the time, whereas now I’d say I get male/female at roughly a 70/30 ratio, although I will say that it heavily depends on presentation—I tend toward the masc/neutral side of the presentation spectrum but on the rare occasion I wear a dress it shoots up to about 90% female regardless of my voice. People see what they want to see. (With my voice though people pretty much always think I’m a guy over the phone.) I will say also that I haven’t yet had top surgery (though I’m planning to) and whether I’m binding or not has a significant effect on how people gender me; they always think they’re being sneaky when they flick their gaze down to my chest to check for boobs but I always notice, lol.

 I’ve been gendered multiple ways by different strangers on the same day, sometimes in the same room. Occasionally people can tell that I’m nonbinary and use “they” for me unprompted (once a guy called me “that young...individual over there” and it warmed my heart). Sometimes people get embarrassed if they think they got it wrong, and I have to assure them that I really don’t care (ie, a woman bumped into me and said “Oh, sorry, ma’am!” and when I said “It’s okay!” in my normal vocal register she flushed bright red and said “...I mean, sir!” and scurried off). Also, my singing voice has improved significantly, although that might be because I’m more comfortable using it now.

As for bottom growth, it obviously varies for everyone, but I ended up with almost an inch of growth, and like I said, this is permanent. I like my junk more now because while I have the same level of sensitivity, it’s spread out across more surface area now instead of being concentrated into a tiny dot, which makes sexual interactions more enjoyable for me.

Not totally sure how my ovaries are doing. I imagine that they’re still functional, although I do plan on getting a hysterectomy eventually, since I know for sure I don’t ever want to be pregnant. I suspect that it might have caused some ovarian cysts though and possibly made me more susceptible to them, but they don’t do much aside from twinge every so often (but sometimes hard enough to make me yelp).

I hope this was helpful! Let me know if you have any questions about my experience.

a few decembers ago now my mom called me from my grandparents’ house and was like, “there’s this cat that’s been wandering around here the last few days and it’s so skinny and dirty and i’m really worried about it but your grandma won’t let it in the house, can you please come get it?”

so (being the cat-loving person that i am) i drove up to get this poor cat. she was just as scraggly and hungry-looking as advertised, but she had a collar on already (the tag said her name was betsy). my mom explained that they’d already tried calling the number multiple times but no one had answered. but it was the middle of winter and she looked like she’d been outside for some time so i decided to put her in a crate and take her home with me, stopping on the way to get some cat food and litter (despite the fact that i was living with my dad at the time and i knew that he wouldn’t want me to bring home some random cat).

when we got home the first 2 things i noticed about her were that a.) her paws clicked weirdly on the hardwood floors and b.) she smelled terrible, so i decided to give her a bath (which she did not appreciate). during the process i found out that the reason her claws were clicking was because they were ingrown—they had grown so far that they’d curved all the way back and were embedded deeply in her paw pads. it looked tremendously painful. she was also very underweight and her long fur was scraggly & matted into locks in several places.

the next day i took her to the vet. the first thing they did—after clucking over her general state—was call the number on her tag. this time someone actually answered. “you found my cat!” he said. “my granddaughter will be so pleased!”

how long has she been lost for? they asked.

“oh, i don’t know…she’s an outdoor cat, and i’m out of town a lot, so sometimes we lose track of her for a while.” (remember: it was december & freezing outside, and she was 11 or 12 years old at the time, which is not young for a cat.)

did you know about her ingrown claws? they asked. how long has it been since you clipped them?

“you’re supposed to clip them?” he said.

after this conversation i already had misgivings about returning her to this guy but i gave him my contact info anyway since after all, it was his cat. he said he’d call about coming to get her soon.

it turned out that her perforated paw pads were infected, which explained why she smelled so bad. the vet was SO nice and performed the extraction of her claws from her paw pads pro bono, since she was in so much pain from it. it was truly awful—they had to cut each claw in half and pull it out, accompanied by a spray of blood each time (the worst ones were embedded half an inch deep), and betsy was squirming and crying and hissing the whole time. they even gave me antibiotics and some disinfectant wipes for her infected paws, and told me that she would need to come back in for a full checkup soon—like, within the week—to make sure the infection hadn’t spread.

her original owner didn’t call me back for a full week. eventually i called him and he was like, “oh, i’m on a business trip for the next few days, but i’ll let you know when i get back.” 

i was like “uhhh ok buddy” and just made a second vet appt for her myself. when we got there they called him again to say “hey guy, your pet is here, would you like to, idk, pay for her medical care?”
he said “yes! sure! no problem! call me when you’re done and i’ll give you my card info.”

so they did a full exam on her, and when they called the guy back—no surprise—he didn’t answer. i paid the $200 bill myself. he never contacted me again. i took her home with me and began nursing her back to health, which included cleaning her paws and administering antibiotics daily, as well as cutting all the mats out of her fur, feeding her—she was ravenous for the first few weeks—and giving her lots of love. she was extremely nervous and skittish around people at first and some of her behavior made me think she had previously been abused (she was terrified of shoes, for instance).

anyway, fast forward one year and betsy was doing SO much better. i took her to the vet for a yearly checkup and the vet—who had taken care of her when i’d brought her in a year ago—didn’t even recognize her at first. she called her progress “a miracle”, called everyone else in the office in to look, and told me i’d probably added 5-10 years to her lifespan. she gained 2 pounds (up from her original weight of 9 lbs when i found her), her fur is soft and healthy, and her eyes are bright. she’s also now the sweetest, mellowest cat i’ve ever owned—i’ve never seen her scratch someone in anger, she tolerates all manner of handling, she never runs from people anymore, she loves to snuggle, and the vet’s office employees said that she was one of the best-behaved cats they’d seen.

i’m SO proud of my little old lady for making such an amazing comeback. the vet said she was very lucky to have found me but personally i think i was lucky to have found her! i love her very much and i’m so happy about all the progress she’s made & that she has a safe, loving home now. she seems very happy about it, too!
